title: Origins of world religions
examples: When and where did Buddhism begin?

explain.say: Historians study how religions began using ancient texts, inscriptions, buildings and archaeology. Along this timeline you can see the world's major religions appear, from roots more than three thousand years old to faiths founded only a few centuries ago.

Religion is far older than writing. Early humans buried their dead with care, and the first cities, in Mesopotamia and Egypt, worshipped many gods in great temples. Those ancient religions have faded, but they shaped the ones that followed.

draw.label: Early sacred sites and temple cities

draw.text: Stonehenge and the pyramids at Giza show how much effort early peoples gave to the sacred.

explain.say: In India, the Vedas, the oldest Hindu scriptures, were composed in Sanskrit more than 3,000 years ago. Over centuries Vedic religion grew into the many traditions we now call Hinduism, which has no single founder.

Between about 800 and 200 BCE, a burst of great teachers appeared in different lands: the Buddha and Mahavira in India, Confucius and Laozi in China, Hebrew prophets in Israel, and philosophers in Greece. Historians call it the Axial Age.

items: Hebrew prophets | Israel and Judah | Judaism

draw.text: Zarathustra, founder of Zoroastrianism in Persia, may be older still; scholars debate his dates.

explain.say: In the Middle East, Judaism grew among the ancient Israelites. Christianity began with Jesus in the first century CE, and Islam began with the Prophet Muhammad in Arabia in the 600s. All three trace their story to Abraham.
Later came Sikhism, begun by Guru Nanak in the Punjab in the 1400s, and the Bahá'í faith in Iran in the 1800s. Here is the whole story in order.

items: over 3,000 years ago: the Vedas; early Judaism

faq.q: When and where did Buddhism begin?
faq.a: Buddhism began in northern India, around the 5th century BCE, with Siddhartha Gautama, the Buddha. He was born at Lumbini in today's Nepal, became enlightened at Bodh Gaya, and taught for about 45 years. Scholars debate his exact dates.

faq.q: When and where did Christianity begin?
faq.a: Christianity began in the first century CE in Judea and Galilee, part of the Roman Empire, with the life and teaching of Jesus, who was crucified in Jerusalem around 30 CE. His followers believed he rose from the dead and spread the faith across the empire.

faq.q: When and where did Islam begin?
faq.a: Islam began in Arabia in the early 600s CE. Muslims believe the Prophet Muhammad received the first revelation of the Qur'an in 610 near Mecca. In 622 he and his followers moved to Medina, the Hijra, and by his death in 632 much of Arabia had become Muslim.

faq.q: When and where did Hinduism begin?
faq.a: Hinduism developed in the Indian subcontinent over thousands of years, with no single founder or start date. Its oldest scriptures, the Vedas, were composed more than 3,000 years ago, and some scholars think certain ideas may reach back to the Indus Valley civilisation, though that is debated.

faq.q: When and where did Judaism begin?
faq.a: Judaism developed among the ancient Israelites in the land of Canaan, later Israel and Judah, more than 3,000 years ago. Jewish tradition traces it to Abraham and to Moses, through whom God gave the Torah. After the Babylonian exile in the 500s BCE, much of the Hebrew Bible took its final shape.

The Axial Age is a name given by the philosopher Karl Jaspers to the period from about 800 to 200 BCE, when influential teachers and thinkers appeared in several regions at once: the Buddha and Mahavira in India, Confucius and Laozi in China, Hebrew prophets in Israel, and philosophers in Greece. Historians still debate how useful the idea is.
asks: why did great teachers appear at the same time

faq.a: No one knows for certain, because religion is older than writing. Careful burials with objects, tens of thousands of years old, suggest early humans had beliefs about death. The first written religions came from Mesopotamia and Egypt, which worshipped many gods.

faq.q: How do historians know how religions began?
faq.a: Historians use sacred texts, other ancient writings, inscriptions such as the rock edicts of the emperor Ashoka, archaeology of temples and burials, and the traditions religions tell about themselves. Where sources are few, they say so, and dates may be debated.
asks: how do we know about ancient religions

faq.a: Sikhism began in the Punjab with Guru Nanak, born in 1469. He taught devotion to one God, equality and service. Nine more human Gurus followed, and in 1708 the tenth, Guru Gobind Singh, named the scripture, the Guru Granth Sahib, as the eternal Guru.

Jainism took its present form with Mahavira in northern India, around the same time as the Buddha. Jains see him as the 24th and last Tirthankara, or ford-maker, of the present age, and believe the teaching itself is eternal.

Zoroastrianism began in ancient Iran with the prophet Zarathustra. Scholars disagree about when he lived, with suggestions ranging from about 1500 to 500 BCE. It became the main religion of the Persian empires and influenced ideas about good and evil and judgement.

faq.q: What religions did ancient Egypt and Mesopotamia have?
faq.a: Both worshipped many gods linked to nature, cities and kingship, such as Ra and Osiris in Egypt and Marduk in Babylon. They built great temples, believed rulers had a special link with the gods, and Egyptians prepared carefully for life after death. These religions are no longer practised, but they influenced later cultures.

Confucianism, based on the teachings of Confucius about 2,500 years ago, focuses on ethics, family and good government. Daoism, linked to Laozi and the Daodejing, seeks harmony with the Dao, the way of nature. Both grew alongside Buddhism, which came from India.

facts: The Vedas, the oldest Hindu scriptures, were composed in Sanskrit more than 3,000 years ago.
The philosopher Karl Jaspers called the period from about 800 to 200 BCE the Axial Age.
Muslims date the first revelation of the Qur'an to 610 CE; the Prophet Muhammad died in 632.
Guru Nanak, the first Sikh Guru, was born in 1469 in the Punjab.
The Bahá'í faith began in Iran in the mid-1800s, with the Báb in 1844 and Bahá'u'lláh in 1863.

quiz.say: Recall. Which period, from about 800 to 200 BCE, saw the Buddha, Confucius and the Hebrew prophets?
quiz.show: The period of the Buddha, Confucius and the Hebrew prophets is called...
quiz.why: Karl Jaspers named the period from about 800 to 200 BCE the Axial Age, when many great teachers appeared.

wrong.1: The Stone Age ended long before these teachers lived.
wrong.2: The Middle Ages came more than a thousand years later.
wrong.3: The Industrial Age began in the 1700s CE.

quiz.say: Apply. Put these in time order, earliest first: Islam, Buddhism, Sikhism.
quiz.why: Buddhism began around 500 BCE, Islam in the 600s CE, and Sikhism in the 1400s CE.

wrong.1: Islam began over a thousand years after the Buddha.
wrong.2: Sikhism is the youngest of the three, not the oldest.

quiz.say: Think. Why do historians often give only approximate dates for when religions began?
quiz.show: Why are origin dates often approximate?

options.show: Early sources are few, and many faiths grew gradually
options.say: Early sources are few, and many faiths grew gradually

options.show: Historians are not interested in dates

quiz.why: Many religions developed over long periods, and early records are scarce, so historians give ranges and note debates.

wrong.1: Dates matter greatly to historians; the problem is the evidence.
wrong.2: Religions began at very different times and places.
